headline: Bank of Canada Holds at 2.25% as May Unemployment Sits at 6.6% and Housing Starts Reach 279,317 SAAR
executive_summary:
The Bank of Canada held the overnight rate at 2.25% on June 10, the second consecutive hold, paired with the June Monetary Policy Report — the 5Y Government of Canada benchmark sits at 3.04%, the residential mortgage-renewal anchor, while the 2s10s spread sits +64 basis points and has bull-flattened over both the one-month and one-year windows.41 All 6,426 active Canadian projects ($1,536.5B aggregate) finance against the GoC yield curve anchored by the policy rate, and 257 residential projects ($36.2B) price renewals against the 5Y tenor.42

Statistics Canada reported real GDP at basic prices contracted 0.1% m/m in March 2026, released May 15, with an April flash estimate of +0.4% — manufacturing (NAICS 31-33) advanced 0.4% m/m but remained -2.5% y/y, while construction (NAICS 23) fell 0.6% m/m and -1.5% y/y.104 The manufacturing reading links to 346 active manufacturing projects ($70.0B); the construction reading links to 1,497 active infrastructure projects ($214.0B).104 Mining and oil and gas (NAICS 21) fell 2.1% m/m and -1.5% y/y, mapping to 532 mining and 89 oil and gas projects totalling $246.6B.104

The May Labour Force Survey, released June 6, recorded the unemployment rate at 6.6%, the participation rate at 65.0%, and the employment rate at 60.7% — average hourly wages fell 1.4% m/m to $37.24, reflecting a composition shift in which accommodation and food employment rose 4.3% m/m to 1,204,200 positions and retail employment fell 1.8% m/m to 2,237,500 positions.105 CMHC reported May housing starts at 279,317 SAAR, up 6.9% m/m, with the April unadjusted total at 21,805 units (+33.0% m/m); the new housing price index fell 0.4% m/m in April, the first negative print after consecutive flat-to-rising months.74

The week ahead carries a dense calendar of releases that will reset the inflation and rate picture — Statistics Canada publishes formal May CPI on June 17, the FOMC announces its rate decision and Summary of Economic Projections the same day under new Chair Kevin Warsh, and the Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee meets June 18 with Bank Rate at 3.75%.1027843 The European Central Bank raised its deposit facility +25 basis points to 2.25% effective June 17, narrowing the ECB-BoC deposit differential to zero.77

national.analysis:
Statistics Canada's March 2026 monthly GDP print, released May 15, recorded a 0.1% m/m contraction at basic prices, with an April advance flash estimate of +0.4% — twenty NAICS industry readings show goods-producing sector weakness concentrated in mining and oil and gas (NAICS 21) at -2.1% m/m and -1.5% y/y, and in construction (NAICS 23) at -0.6% m/m and -1.5% y/y, against services-producing strength in wholesale trade (+1.8% m/m), arts, entertainment and recreation (+2.0% m/m), and public administration (+0.4% m/m).104 Manufacturing (NAICS 31-33) advanced 0.4% m/m but remained -2.5% y/y, linking to 346 active manufacturing projects ($70.0B) in the project database.104

The May Labour Force Survey, released June 6, recorded unemployment at 6.6%, unchanged m/m, with the participation rate at 65.0% and the employment rate at 60.7% — sector employment shifted toward lower-wage industries, with accommodation and food rising 4.3% m/m to 1,204,200, agriculture rising 8.6% m/m to 240,100, and construction rising 0.5% m/m, while retail trade fell 1.8% m/m to 2,237,500, manufacturing fell 0.5% m/m to 243,200, and mining and oil and gas fell 0.5% m/m to 343,000.105 Average hourly wages fell 1.4% m/m to $37.24, a reading consistent with the composition shift.108

Manufacturing sales reached $77,052.9 million in April, up 4.2% m/m, and wholesale trade reached $138,830.0 million, up 2.8% m/m — both readings sit above their three-month moving averages and link respectively to 346 manufacturing and to broader transport and warehousing project flows tracked across 628 active projects ($54.0B).110113 April merchandise exports stood at $66.3 billion per the StatCan section, with energy exports up 9.7% m/m to $19.88 billion and agri-food exports up 8.9% m/m, while mineral exports fell 7.9% m/m.106 The energy export strength sits against a WTI tape down 11.7% w/w to $80.58/bbl, which the cross-reference engine links to 89 active oil and gas projects ($63.2B).21

CMHC reported May housing starts at 279,317 SAAR, up 6.9% m/m from 261,377 SAAR in April, with the April unadjusted total at 21,805 units (singles 3,063, multi 18,742) — multi-unit starts rose 34.3% m/m and single starts rose 25.4% m/m relative to March.74 Residential permits fell 5.5% m/m to $7,482.9 million and non-residential permits fell 10.5% m/m to $5,008.2 million in April per Statistics Canada 34-10-0292, while the new housing price index fell 0.4% m/m to 121.1 in April, the first negative print after flat-to-rising months.118112 The headline housing starts reading links to 257 residential projects ($36.2B) in the project database.74

Statistics Canada's quarterly household income, consumption and saving release for Q1 2026 recorded the household savings rate at 3.5%, down 0.2 percentage points q/q from 3.7% in Q4 2025, with household disposable income at $1,811,968 million (+0.6% q/q) — non-residential capital expenditure intentions for 2026 stand at $401,203 million, up 3.7% y/y per Statistics Canada 34-10-0035.115119 The Department of Finance Spring Economic Update 2026 set out $51 billion in infrastructure commitments alongside a new sovereign fund and an expansion of the Investment Tax Credit to cover CCUS-EOR, which the cross-reference engine maps against 1,497 active infrastructure projects ($214.0B) and the broader power and energy sector that tracks 936 active projects ($614.3B).226

goodsIndustries.analysis:
Agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting GDP eased 1.1% month-over-month against a +2.1% year-over-year reading for the March reference month — the monthly softening81 sits against a backdrop of firmer farm-gate prices, with the Saskatchewan canola farm price at CAD$672.81/t in April, up 6.2% year-over-year and 1.8% month-over-month18. Potash proxy Nutrien closed the week at $92.23, up 12.0% year-over-year but down 1.9% week-over-week, easing one input-cost line for Prairie producers while keeping the annual comparison elevated72.

The Agriculture and Forestry pipeline tracks 733 active projects at $8.2B in priced value, split $3.5B agriculture and $4.7B forestry — the Canada Food Security Strategy35, a $3.2B Ontario-led federal program, was added at Proposed status on 2026-06-11, while Drake Meat Processors entered Under Construction in Saskatoon and Atlas Engineered Products Advanced Wood Manufacturing Facility in Clinton, Ontario, reached Approved status this week95.

If canola holds above CAD$670/t and the potash month-over-month softening continues, Prairie farm-gate margins would see input relief into Q3 — only 2 of 464 priced Agriculture rows carry stated values, so the directional read is from commodities and named additions rather than aggregate dollars36. Procurement.json has been empty for eight consecutive weeks, removing visibility into federal agri-program contract awards95.

Glencore Horne Smelter Emissions Reduction was filed at $300M proposed in Quebec, sitting at the NAICS 21/31-33 boundary95.

The divergence between -2.1% month-over-month output and +111.6% year-over-year nickel suggests volume declines and IAAC review pauses are outweighing price-driven revenue gains in the StatCan series — if nickel and iron ore hold near current levels, breakeven economics for the 651 mining-tagged projects shift, and the Eranova, FireFly, and Glencore Horne files would advance through IAAC and provincial environmental assessment more readily36. consumer_pulse:
Headline CPI sits at +2.8% y/y on the May reference snapshot while average hourly wages fell 1.4% m/m to $37.24 in the May Labour Force Survey — the gap between price and wage readings continues to surface in cost-of-living trackers, with cost of living, housing affordability, and inflation among the highest-frequency topics this week.105102 The household savings rate fell to 3.5% in Q1 2026 from 3.7% in Q4 2025 per Statistics Canada 36-10-0112, the lowest reading in two quarters.119

Mortgage and housing-cost signals dominate the consumer picture — the 5Y Government of Canada yield at 3.04% is the residential mortgage-renewal anchor, down 15 basis points y/y, while the new housing price index fell 0.4% m/m in April, the first negative print after flat-to-rising months.41112 CMHC reported May housing starts at 279,317 SAAR, up 6.9% m/m, with multi-unit starts up 34.3% m/m relative to March.74

Energy and food prices shape the goods basket — WTI crude fell 11.7% w/w to $80.58/bbl from $105.42 a month ago, a partial reversal of the recent supply-shock premium, with pass-through to retail gasoline pending.21 Sector employment shifted toward lower-wage industries, with accommodation and food up 4.3% m/m and retail down 1.8% m/m in May, a composition that helps explain the m/m drop in average hourly wages.105 The Department of Finance Spring Economic Update 2026 committed $51 billion in infrastructure spending, established a new sovereign fund, and expanded the Investment Tax Credit to CCUS-EOR, signals that show up in the federal budget and infrastructure topics tracked across the week.2

yieldCurveCommentary: The Government of Canada yield curve held a normal slope on June 12 with the 2s10s spread at +64 basis points — the 10Y benchmark sat at 3.40% versus the 2Y at 2.76%, after the Bank of Canada's June 10 decision to hold the overnight rate at 2.25% for the second consecutive meeting alongside the June Monetary Policy Report.41 Year-over-year, the 2Y has risen 5 basis points from 2.71%, the 5Y 8 basis points from 2.96% to 3.04%, the 10Y 3 basis points from 3.37%, and the long bond 17 basis points from 3.65% to 3.82%, reflecting greater term-premium pickup at the back end than the front.21 The 5Y benchmark at 3.04% remains the residential mortgage-renewal anchor cited in the June MPR.42 The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine ties the curve to 6,426 active Canadian projects ($1,536.5B aggregate) financed against the GoC term structure, with 257 residential projects ($36.2B) most directly exposed to 5Y pricing for mortgage refinancing.21 If the 5Y benchmark holds above three percent through the third quarter, the 257 residential projects would face renewal pricing 8 basis points wider than the year-ago benchmark, while the 1,497 active infrastructure projects priced off the 10Y would carry roughly 3 basis points of additional carry versus the same window in 2025.21
